title: SQL Joins
description: Test your knowledge of joining tables in SQL

questions.question: What is the purpose of a JOIN in SQL?
options: To delete rows from a table
To combine rows from two or more tables
To sort rows in a table
questions.explanation: JOIN combines rows from two or more tables based on a related column.

questions.question: Which JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table.

questions.question: What does INNER JOIN return?
options: Rows from the right table only
Rows with matching values in both tables
Rows from the left table only
questions.explanation: INNER JOIN returns only the rows with matching values in both tables.

questions.question: Which JOIN returns all rows from both tables, with NULLs where no match exists?
questions.explanation: FULL JOIN returns all rows from both tables, filling in NULLs for non-matches.

questions.question: What is the default JOIN type if just 'JOIN' is specified?
questions.explanation: If only 'JOIN' is specified, it defaults to INNER JOIN.

questions.question: Which clause is used to specify the condition for joining tables?
questions.explanation: The ON clause specifies the condition for joining tables.

questions.question: What is a self-join?
questions.explanation: A self-join is when a table is joined to itself, often to compare rows within the same table.

questions.question: Which JOIN type is the opposite of LEFT JOIN?
questions.explanation: RIGHT JOIN is the opposite of LEFT JOIN, returning all rows from the right table and matched rows from the left.

questions.question: What does CROSS JOIN produce?
options: A Cartesian product of the tables
questions.explanation: CROSS JOIN produces a Cartesian product, combining all rows from both tables.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to join tables based on columns with the same name?
questions.explanation: The USING keyword simplifies joins when columns in both tables have the same name.
